site.name: Tidewrack Studio Pottery
site.tagline: Thrown and glazed by hand on the quay at Harrowby
site.address: The Net Loft, Quay Row, Harrowby
site.hours: Studio shop open Thursday to Saturday, 10am to 4pm
site.demo_note: A fictional pottery in the made-up town of Harrowby, built as a demonstration for newsroom.sgit.ai. The maker, the pieces and the prices are invented.

maker.name: Nell Carrow
paragraphs: Nell Carrow throws stoneware in an old net loft on Quay Row, a few steps from the harbour wall. The studio window looks out over the tideline, and most of the glazes are named after what the sea leaves behind.

Every piece is thrown on the wheel or built by hand, trimmed, bisque fired, glazed and fired again to stoneware temperature. Glazes are mixed in the studio from local wood ash and a few plain minerals, so each batch comes out a little different.

There is no online shop. The catalogue below shows what is on the shelves this season. If something catches your eye, enquire in the studio and Nell will tell you if it is still there, or when the next firing is.

tidewrack.name: Tidewrack green
tidewrack.note: A layered ash glaze that breaks brown on the edges, like weed left on the sand.

oyster.name: Oyster white
oyster.note: A soft satin white with a little iron speckle showing through.

harbour.name: Harbour blue
harbour.note: A deep cobalt and iron blue that pools darker in the hollows.

ironred.name: Iron red
ironred.note: A warm iron glaze that goes rust red where it runs thick.

kelp.name: Kelp brown
kelp.note: A glossy tenmoku style brown, almost black on the rims.

seaglass.name: Sea glass
seaglass.note: A pale celadon that collects in the throwing lines.

slate.name: Slate
slate.note: A matt grey stone glaze, quiet and very hard wearing.

honey.name: Honey ash
honey.note: A runny amber glaze with drips that stop just short of the foot.

enquiry: There is no checkout and no contact form on this site, by design: it is a simple static catalogue. To ask about a piece, enquire in the studio. Quote the reference number and Nell will tell you if it is still on the shelf, or when the next firing is due.

classes.title: Wheel taster evening
classes.text: Your first go on the wheel. Throw a few cylinders and bowls; Nell trims, glazes and fires the one you like most.

classes.title: Six week throwing course
classes.text: Centring, opening, pulling walls, trimming and handles. You glaze your own pieces in week six. Clay and firing included.

classes.title: Hand building weekend
classes.text: Pinch, coil and slab. Make a set of small dishes and one larger piece. No wheel needed.

classes.title: Glazing afternoon
classes.text: For past students. Learn how the studio glazes are mixed and layered, and glaze your bisque ware.

open_days.title: Winter open studio
open_days.text: Seconds shelf, mulled apple juice, and the kiln opened at 11am.

open_days.title: Last firing before the holidays
open_days.text: Collect pieces from the taster evenings and see the new moon jars.

open_days.title: Spring open studio
open_days.text: Throwing demonstrations every hour and a look round the glaze room.

open_days.title: Harbour day open studio
open_days.text: The studio doors open onto the quay for the town harbour day.

care.title: Dishwasher
care.text: Mugs, bowls and plates are fired to stoneware and can go in the dishwasher. Hand washing keeps the glaze bright for longer.

care.title: Microwave
care.text: Plain glazed pieces are fine in the microwave. Pieces with iron red or kelp brown glazes can get hot at the rim, so take care.

care.title: Oven
care.text: Bowls and plates can warm in a low oven. Put them in cold and let them heat up with the oven, and avoid sudden changes of temperature.

care.title: Unglazed feet
care.text: The bare clay on the foot of each piece can mark a table. A dab of beeswax, or a felt pad, stops it scratching.

care.title: Vases
care.text: Vases are glazed inside and hold water. Empty and dry them now and then so the water line does not stain.

care.title: Chips and cracks
care.text: Stoneware is tough, not unbreakable. If a piece chips at the rim, stop using it for drinking and bring it to the studio to look at.
